slides.heading: Youngest Common Ancestor
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Youngest Common Ancestor, a medium graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Nodes have only an `ancestor` pointer; find the deepest common ancestor of two descendants.
Equalise depths, then walk up together.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Nodes have only an ancestor pointer; find the deepest common ancestor of two descendants. Equalise depths, then walk up together.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Bring both descendants to the same depth, then climb together until they meet.
slides.narration: Bring both descendants to the same depth, then climb together until they meet.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Store all ancestors of one node in a set, walk up the other → O(d) space
Equalise depths, then climb together → O(d) time, O(1) space
d = depth of the deeper node
slides.narration: One approach stores all of one node's ancestors in a set, then walks up from the other until it finds one. Equalising depths and then climbing both in lockstep avoids extra memory.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, compute both depths. Second, lift the deeper one. Third, move both up until equal.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Descendants E and I; depths 2 and 3
slides.narration: Find the youngest common ancestor of E and I. E is at depth two, I at depth three.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Lift the deeper one: I → D
slides.narration: First lift the deeper node, I, by one level to D, so both are at depth two.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Move both up: E → B, D → B → answer B
slides.narration: Now move both up together. E goes to B, D goes to B. They meet: the answer is B.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We compute both depths by walking up to the top. Then we lift the deeper node until depths match, and finally move both up together until they're the same node.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of d. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: One node is the ancestor of the other
The answer may be the top ancestor
slides.narration: If one node is the ancestor of the other, the algorithm returns it naturally. The same node twice returns itself.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: binary tree without parent pointers (LCA)
slides.narration: Without parent pointers, use the recursive lowest common ancestor. For many queries, binary lifting answers each in log time.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Bring both descendants to the same depth, then climb together until they meet.
slides.narration: To recap Youngest Common Ancestor: Bring both descendants to the same depth, then climb together until they meet. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
